body.statement:
Fix \(\mathcal A\) and \(M\), and let \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) use finitely many cylinders.  Assume \(F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)\), strict stationarity, cylinder positivity, \(\beta_M(k)\le C_\beta\rho^k\), the Bartlett kernel, \(h_T\to\infty\), \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), and \(v_F>0\).  Define \(\widehat\theta_F\) and \(\widehat v_F\) on the event that their empirical denominators are positive, and arbitrarily off that event.  Then that event has probability tending to one,
\[
 \widehat\Omega_F\overset p\longrightarrow\Omega_F,\qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_F-\theta_M(y;x))\Rightarrow N(0,v_F),\qquad
 \widehat v_F\overset p\longrightarrow v_F,
\]
and
\[
 P_M\!\left\{\theta_M(y;x)\in
 \left[\widehat\theta_F\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_F/T}\right]\right\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
Algebraically equivalent cylinder expressions have the same limit after redundant simplex coordinates are removed.
body.proof_tex:
Let \([a_j,b_j]\) be the smallest integer interval containing all time indices in the \(j\)-th cylinder, after placing that cylinder at shift zero, and put \(w=\max_j(b_j-a_j)<\infty\).  Then \(Z_t\) is measurable with respect to the observed variables from time \(t+\min_j a_j\) through time \(t+\max_j b_j\).  Consequently the absolute-regularity coefficients of \((Z_t)\) satisfy
\[
 \beta_Z(k)\le \beta_M((k-w)_+)\le C_\beta\rho^{(k-w)_+}.
\]
Indeed, the past and future sigma fields generated by the two \(Z\)-blocks are subfields of observed-process sigma fields separated by at least \(k-w\), and absolute regularity decreases when sigma fields are restricted.  Since every coordinate of \(Z_t\) lies in \([0,1]\), the total-variation definition of \(\beta\) gives, for bounded scalar functions \(G,H\) of blocks separated by \(k\),
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}(G,H)|
 \le4\lVert G\rVert_\infty\lVert H\rVert_\infty\beta_Z(k).
\]
Thus every entry of \(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Cov}(Z_0,Z_k)\) is absolutely summable, so \(\Omega_F\) is finite.  The same covariance bound yields
\[
 E\lVert\widehat p_F-p_F\rVert^2=O(T^{-1}),
\]
where omitting the fixed cylinder boundary changes the mean by only \(O(T^{-1})\).  Hence \(\widehat p_F-p_F=O_p(T^{-1/2})\).

For completeness, a blocking argument gives the required multivariate central limit theorem from these stated assumptions.  Fix a vector \(c\) and put \(W_t=c^{\mathsf T}(Z_t-p_F)\).  Let the big-block length be \(b_T=\lfloor T^{1/5}\rfloor\), let the separating gap be \(s_T=\lceil d\log T\rceil\), where \(d>2/|\log\rho|\), and partition \(1,\ldots,T\) into big blocks separated by such gaps.  Absolute covariance summability shows that the variance of the sum over all gaps, divided by \(T\), is \(O(s_T/b_T)=o(1)\).  If \(m_T\) is the number of big blocks, iterative use of the total-variation definition gives, for the joint characteristic function of their sums and the product of their marginal characteristic functions, the bound
\[
 2(m_T-1)\beta_Z(s_T)
 \le C\frac{T}{b_T}\rho^{s_T-w}=o(1).
\]
It therefore suffices to analyze independent random variables having the big-block-sum marginals.  Absolute covariance summability also gives
\[
 \frac1T\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{t=1}^T W_t\right)
 \longrightarrow
 \sigma_c^2:=c^{\mathsf T}\Omega_Fc,
\]
and removing the gaps does not change this limit.  Each centered big-block sum is bounded by \(C b_T\).  Taylor's formula for its characteristic function has total third-order remainder bounded by
\[
 \frac{C b_T}{T^{3/2}}\sum_{j=1}^{m_T}\operatorname{Var}(B_{T,j})
 =O(b_TT^{-1/2})=o(1).
\]
The quadratic terms converge to \(-u^2\sigma_c^2/2\), and their maximal magnitude is \(O(b_T/T)=o(1)\); taking the product therefore yields \(\exp(-u^2\sigma_c^2/2)\).  Restoring the negligible gaps proves
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt T}\sum_{t=1}^T W_t\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma_c^2).
\]
Since \(c\) was arbitrary, the corresponding characteristic-function identity proves
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat p_F-p_F)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_F).
\]

We next prove HAC consistency.  Write \(U_t=Z_t-p_F\), \(\Gamma_k=E(U_tU_{t-k}^{\mathsf T})\), and
\[
 \widetilde\Gamma_k=T^{-1}\sum_{t=k+1}^TU_tU_{t-k}^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For any matrix entry, the product at time \(t\) and the product at time \(t+r\) are bounded.  When \(r>k+w\), their underlying observed blocks are separated by at least \(r-k-w\); the covariance inequality above applies.  For the remaining \(k+w+1\) separations use the bound by one.  Uniformly for \(0\le k<T\),
\[
 E\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_k-E\widetilde\Gamma_k\rVert
 \le C\sqrt{\frac{k+w+1}{T}}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 E\sum_{k=0}^{h_T}\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_k-E\widetilde\Gamma_k\rVert
 \le C\frac{h_T^{3/2}}{\sqrt T}=o(1),
\]
because \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\).  Also \(E\widetilde\Gamma_k=(1-k/T)\Gamma_k\).  Since \(h_T\to\infty\), the Bartlett weights converge to one at each fixed lag, are bounded by one, and \(\sum_k\lVert\Gamma_k\rVert<\infty\).  Splitting the sum at a fixed lag and then sending that lag to infinity gives
\[
 \widetilde\Gamma_0+
 \sum_{k=1}^{h_T}K(k/(h_T+1))
 (\widetilde\Gamma_k+\widetilde\Gamma_k^{\mathsf T})
 \overset p\longrightarrow\Omega_F.
\]
Finally, with \(d_T=\widehat p_F-p_F\), replacing \(U_t\) by \(U_t-d_T\) changes each empirical lag covariance by at most \(C(\lVert d_T\rVert+\lVert d_T\rVert^2)\).  Summed over \(h_T\) lags this is \(O_p(h_TT^{-1/2})=o_p(1)\).  Hence \(\widehat\Omega_F\overset p\to\Omega_F\).

Every denominator of \(F\) is positive at \(p_F\).  There are finitely many denominators, so all remain positive on some neighborhood of \(p_F\).  Since \(\widehat p_F\to_p p_F\), the empirical-domain event has probability tending to one.  On this neighborhood the rational map \(F\) is twice continuously differentiable, and Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \sqrt T\{F(\widehat p_F)-F(p_F)\}
 =\nabla F(p_F)^{\mathsf T}\sqrt T(\widehat p_F-p_F)+o_p(1).
\]
Using the assumed identifying equality \(F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)\) and the vector central limit theorem yields the stated normal limit with variance
\[
 v_F=\nabla F(p_F)^{\mathsf T}\Omega_F\nabla F(p_F).
\]
Continuity of \(\nabla F\), consistency of \(\widehat p_F\), and HAC consistency imply \(\widehat v_F\to_p v_F\).  Since \(v_F>0\), studentization and continuity of the standard normal distribution give
\[
 P_M\!\left\{\theta_M(y;x)\in
 \left[\widehat\theta_F\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_F/T}\right]\right\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]

For the final invariance assertion, remove linearly redundant cylinder cells and use coordinates on the relative interior of the resulting probability simplex.  Algebraically equivalent rational expressions agree on an open subset of those coordinates, so their gradients there agree.  Equivalently, before reduction their gradient difference is normal to the affine support of \(Z_t-p_F\), and hence is annihilated by \(\Omega_F\).  Their linear delta-method terms and quadratic variance forms are therefore identical.
